evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-13"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-13". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. Dates are plain YYYY-MM-DD strings. A datetime string such as 2026-10-14T10:00:00Z was rejected with 400.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-11-01"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH /todos/1 with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. A later GET /todos showed both changes.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30" returned 400. POST with "14/10/2026" returned 400. POST with a datetime string returned 400. PATCH with "2026-02-30" returned 400. PATCH with "x" returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Test data, with today = 2026-10-14: past 2026-10-13, today 2026-10-14, future 2026-10-15, one with no date, one with a past date that I marked done, and old 2025-12-31. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only 'past' and 'old'. The due-today, future, no-date and done todos were excluded.
evidence.AC5: Loaded / in the browser. Each todo with a date showed it, e.g. 'past fällig 13.10.2026', 'today fällig 14.10.2026', 'future fällig 15.10.2026', 'none fällig 01.11.2026'. The todo with no date showed no date text in the earlier GET; it was set later in the run.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, 'past fällig 13.10.2026 überfällig' and 'old fällig 31.12.2025 überfällig' carried the word. The due-today, future, undated and done todos ('pastdone ✓ fällig 01.01.2026') did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list from 6 items to only 'past' and 'old', the two overdue todos.
